summary: 630-line open-source project released March 2026 that closes a research loop by having an agent propose, run, and validate code changes in a tight loop, keeping only improvements. Ran 700 experiments in 2 days and discovered 20 optimizations. Concept: self-improving agent loop with hard evaluation gate before committing changes.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already does skill distillation post-run (distillationAgent.ts). The 'commit only if better' loop pattern is interesting but requires a measurable benchmark, which AgentForge doesn't have for issue resolution quality. HID-188 tracks cross-run episodic memory injection. Backlog is at capacity (10 open issues); blocked from creating issue even if it passed scoring.

summary: Open-sourced August 6, 2026. RLM (Recursive Language Model) architecture with a Continual Harness — skills ship as importable Python packages inside a persistent IPython kernel. Sub-agents are function calls. Reports 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (ProcessRunner) not an embedded REPL kernel; the architecture is fundamentally different. The 'skills as code packages' concept is interesting but conflicts with AgentForge's markdown/YAML skill format. Not implementable without rewriting ProcessRunner. Backlog also at capacity.

source: CODESKILL: Learning Self-Evolving Skills for Coding Agents
summary: May 2026 arXiv paper. RL-based framework that extracts multi-granularity procedural skills from coding-agent trajectories, evolves skills with new experience, and maintains a compact skill bank. Reports +9.69pp pass rate improvement on SWE-Bench Verified over no-skill baseline.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly related to AgentForge's existing distillation pipeline (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The 'skill bank evolution' concept aligns with the known gap that executor prompts don't receive skills (partially tracked by HID-188). However RL training loop is a hard red flag per evaluation rules, and HID-188 covers the executor skill injection angle. Backlog at capacity.

source: Episodic-Semantic Memory Architecture for Long-Horizon Scientific Agents (arXiv 2605.17625)
summary: May 2026 arXiv paper proposing a dual-process memory architecture: episodic (FIFO sliding window) + semantic (structured entity-level abstractions). MAGMA architecture scored highest on LoCoMo benchmark (0.7 judge score) vs MemoryOS (0.553) and A-MEM (0.58).
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — HID-188 already explicitly tracks 'inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts'. The specific MAGMA architecture adds detail but the capability gap is already captured. Creating another issue on this theme would be a duplicate.

summary: April 2026 release of LangGraph with improved durable checkpointing, native DAG workflows, and human-in-the-loop interrupt points. Positioned as the enterprise default for stateful multi-agent orchestration with persistent state across restarts.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge implements its own deterministic state machine (stateMachine.ts) with an explicit transition table. LangGraph's graph-based patterns are interesting but the core features (durable state, human-in-the-loop approvals) already exist in AgentForge's design. Not a gap worth addressing.

summary: AutoGen 1.0 General Availability released February 2026, promoting v2's event-driven multi-agent architecture to stable. Unified with Semantic Kernel as Microsoft Agent Framework (announced Oct 2025). Supports graph-based workflows and concurrent agent execution.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge deliberately uses sequential CLI subprocess execution (not parallel/event-driven). Phase 2 documentation notes parallel agent execution is a deliberate non-goal for now. AutoGen's concurrent agent patterns would require a fundamental architecture change.

source: EU AI Act August 2026 enforcement — agent audit trail requirements
summary: EU AI Act enforcement activated August 2, 2026. Article 12 mandates tamper-evident logging of all agent decisions, 6-month log retention minimum, human oversight mechanisms. 82% of enterprises have undiscovered agents. Penalties up to €35M or 7% of revenue.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already logs orchestration steps via pino. The compliance angle could justify enhancing log retention/audit trail features. However HID-163 already tracks token/cost telemetry which is the primary observability gap. An audit-trail issue would need to be scoped carefully to not duplicate HID-163; backlog at capacity prevents creating now.

summary: February 2026 talk where Karpathy coins 'agentic engineering': orchestrating agents as oversight rather than direct coding. Conceptual framing for how human-AI collaboration works in 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — conceptual framing without a concrete implementation pattern to adopt. AgentForge already embodies the human-in-the-loop oversight model (AwaitingPlanApproval, HumanClarificationNeeded states). No actionable gap identified.

summary: CrewAI 1.14.3 (April 2026) stable release; v0.95 (February 2026) added experimental async crew runner and improved Anthropic/Google model tool-call routing. Supports native MCP and A2A protocols.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses its own CLI-subprocess model, not a crew/role-based framework. Async execution is a deliberate non-goal. MCP/A2A protocol support is irrelevant to AgentForge's current agent-dispatch pattern.
